## Summary

Set up a complete failover routing chain in the proxy where requests try Qwen3 locally first, then fall back to OpenCode Zen free tier (deepseek-v4-flash-free), then OpenCode Go (deepseek-v4-flash). Configure Pi to connect to this proxy and use the failover model.

## User Story

As a developer using the LLM proxy, I want to send a single request and have it automatically try local Qwen3 first. If no slots are available, fall back to a free remote model. If that is rate-limited, fall back to a paid remote model.

## Context

- The proxy config entry `qwen3-fallback` was partially added in `proxy/config.yaml` with three providers (local-qwen3, opencode-deepseek-free, opencode-go-deepseek)
- `proxy/proxy_remote.py` was modified to support the `model` field for upstream model name override
- A bug exists in `proxy/proxy/ui.py` where `_extract_router_model_ids` is called without being imported (NameError)
- Pi needs to be configured to connect to the proxy with the failover model as available

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The `_extract_router_model_ids` NameError bug in `ui.py` is fixed
2. The proxy reloads successfully with the `qwen3-fallback` model entry
3. A request to `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: qwen3-fallback` returns a response (from whichever provider succeeds)
4. The response includes an `X-Provider` header identifying which provider served the request
5. Pi is configured to use the proxy with the failover model as one of its available models
6. All existing tests still pass
data.title: Complete failover plan configuration with Pi instance integration

# Set cheap-mode local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold to 38000 (re-attempt after 60000 revert)

## Problem statement

The original mode-aware raise (LP-0MSOMVOPH004ATAK) set cheap cold to 60000; post-deploy validation (LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K) showed it breached the queue guardrails on 3 of 4 nights (fallback_after_queue 322/338/180 vs 2x baseline ~230; sustained depth-4 samples in the 01:00-03:00 peak) and it was reverted to 30000 (git 0a9bd1d). The parent item cannot close: AC1's literal "cheap 30000->60000" sub-clause is unmet and AC6 (cheap guardrails hold) is unverified post-revert.

A data-backed re-analysis (comment on LP-0MSOMVOPH004ATAK, Aug 10-18 cheap-window logs) identified the safe operating envelope: the 2-slot cheap queue saturates at arrivals >~300/night (60s max-wait expiry cascade); congestion concentrates in 01:00-03:00 (deploy/boot + cold-cache peak). The per-night flip (requests recaptured to local) at each candidate threshold is: 38000 -> 20-38, 42000 -> 33-44, 46000 -> 52-53, 60000 -> 65-94 (worst night 189). Revision: set cheap cold to 38000 (same value as fast/default), which stays well inside the safe envelope and keeps the (38K, 100K] dead-code band intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. config-cheap.yaml `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` set to 38000 (from 30000), with the config comment updated to document the 60000->30000->38000 history (LP-0MSOMVOPH004ATAK / LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K) and the reason 38000 is safe (below cheap warm 100000, below boot-transient clamp 61440, flip 20-38/night).
2. Tests updated: test_mode_config.py asserts cheap cold == 38000; test_ctx_slot_validation.py band-collapse validation still passes with cheap cold 38000 < warm 100000 (band (38K, 100K] non-empty); existing (30K,60K] recapture test adjusted to the 38000 band; full test suite passes.
3. Post-deploy: after 2 cheap windows (01:00-10:00) with the new value live, extract from /var/log/llama-proxy (same method as LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K): routing_skip_local / Fallback triggered / status_request contention fields per night.
4. Guardrails hold for both monitored nights: nightly contention_fallback_after_queue_count delta < 2x baseline (<=230) AND no sustained depth-4 samples (max transient depth-4 <= ~10 samples, none sustained >~10 min) in the 01:00-03:00 peak.
5. REVERT trigger: if either guardrail is breached on 2 consecutive nights, revert cheap cold to 30000, re-run the validation, and comment results on the parent LP-0MSOMVOPH004ATAK.
6. Results (recapture rate, guardrail metrics, keep/revert decision) commented on LP-0MSOMVOPH004ATAK as the AC6 closure evidence.

## Notes

- Congestion history: all depth-4 samples on failing nights occurred 01:00-03:00 (deply/boot + cold-cache peak); 04:00-10:00 was fine at every threshold tested.
- Fast mode at 38000 has zero guardrail events in all fast windows Aug 13-17 - the value itself is operationally proven; the remaining risk is cheap-mode 2-slot capacity.
- Counters are cumulative since proxy process start; compute per-night deltas per proxy session (resets possible - Aug 14 had a mid-window restart).
- Do NOT raise to >=46000 (measured flip 52-53/night typical, up to 108 on busy nights - inside the proven failure envelope of the 60000 experiments).

## Key Files
- `proxy/config-cheap.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_mode_config.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_ctx_slot_validation.py`
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (validation logs)
data.title: Set cheap-mode cold threshold to 38000 with 2-window guardrail validation (re-attempt after 60000 revert)

# Set cheap-mode local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold to 42000 (from 38000) with guardrail validation

## Problem statement

Decision pinned from the safe-level investigation (LP-0MT50SMU1005ZAD6): raise the cheap-mode large-context cold-cache threshold from 38000 to **42000**. Data (LP-0MSY0V4ZO002ANPL measured flips): 38000 → 20-38 recaptured-to-local requests/night, 42000 → 33-44, 46000 → 52-53, 60000 → 65-94 (worst 189). The 60000 experiment (LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K) failed on contention guardrails (`contention_fallback_after_queue` 315/335 vs ≤230 baseline, sustained depth-4 in the 01:00-03:00 peak) and the documented envelope is **do not raise ≥ 46000**; 42000 stays inside the safe region with comfortable margins:

- 42000 < cheap warm clamp 100000 (262144//2 - 4096 = 126976, min → 100000)
- 42000 < boot-transient clamp 61440
- (42000, 100000] band stays non-empty (dead-code guard LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP)
- Arrival headroom: ~33-44 flips/night vs ~≤300/night safe envelope; expected recapture gain over 38000 = ~5-16 more sessions/night kept local (the 2026-08-22 overnight analysis found 384 bypasses in 04:00-06:00, median est. 56.5k tokens — many fall in the (38k, 42k] band).

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — more overnight traffic kept local (no remote cost, fewer 429-induced stalls) without re-triggering cheap-mode queue contention.
- **Herdr Context Hub** — 04:00-06:00 audit batches whose cold prompts currently bypass local.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `proxy/config-cheap.yaml` → `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` set to **42000**, config comment updated: 60000→30000→38000→42000 history (LP-0MSOMVOPH004ATAK / LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K / LP-0MSY0V4ZO002ANPL / LP-0MT50SMU1005ZAD6), why 42000 is safe (below warm 100000 and boot clamp 61440, band (42000, 100000] non-empty, flips 33-44/night), and the do-not-raise-≥-46000 boundary.
2. Tests updated: `proxy/tests/test_mode_config.py` (cheap cold 38000 → 42000 assertion, symmetric-with-fast note dropped/adjusted since fast stays 38000), `proxy/tests/test_ctx_slot_validation.py` band-collapse test still passes (cold 42000 < warm 100000), any (38k, …] band/re-capture tests adjusted to the new band; full suite green.
3. Fast mode unchanged (stays 38000) — cheap-only change.
4. Post-deploy: after 2 cheap windows (01:00-10:00) extract from /var/log/llama-proxy (LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K method): nightly `routing_skip_local`/`Fallback triggered`/`contention_fallback_after_queue` fields; record actual recapture count.
5. Guardrails hold both nights: nightly contention_fallback_after_queue delta < 2x baseline (≤ 230) AND no sustained depth-4 samples in the 01:00-03:00 peak.
6. REVERT trigger: if either guardrail breaches 2 consecutive nights, revert cheap cold to 38000, re-run validation, comment results (LP-0MSY0V4ZO002ANPL AC5 pattern).
7. Results (recapture rate, guardrail metrics, keep/revert decision) commented on this item and referenced on LP-0MT50SMU1005ZAD6.

## Notes

- Implementation must happen in a worktree per the implement skill (`implement.py start LP-0MT50SMU1005ZAD6` is the investigation parent; this item is the pinned decision — if worktrees pair items, use this item's id).
- Coordination: if the Herdr dispatch-concurrency/cadence items (WL-0MT50LKAK001EF5Q, WL-0MT50SAYC005AW85) land before this validation completes, re-run the 2-window guardrail check after both ship — they change the cheap-window arrival profile and may shift the safe envelope.
- tiktoken ~1.69x undercount caveat (LP-0MSEGPO77005CYCQ) is unchanged by this raise: 42000 estimated stays far below the physical per-slot cap (~131072), so no new KV-overflow risk.
- Related: LP-0MT50SMU1005ZAD6 (safe-level investigation, discovered-from), LP-0MSY0V4ZO002ANPL (38000 re-attempt, flip data source), LP-0MSRM54YO007YG0K (60000 validation/revert protocol), LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP (band-collapse guard).

data.description:
## Problem

When the proxy returns a 503 'All providers exhausted' response, retry_after is **hardcoded to 60 seconds**. The Worklog extension's retry loop then waits 2 seconds, retries, fails again, and loops for up to ~60 seconds with exponential backoff — all while real provider availability is **minutes to hours away** (big-pickle cooldown: 86400s; go-2 reset: Aug 30; deepseek: outside available_times).

This wastes time and produces repeated error notifications that confuse the user.

## Solution

The proxy already collects per-provider availability data in unavailable_providers (cooldown maps) and knows about available_times windows. Compute the **real next-available time** and emit it as:

1. **A Retry-After HTTP header** (standard mechanism, integer seconds until retry is valid)
2. **The retry_after field** in the JSON response (already exists but is wrong)

### Implementation details

The proxy response is built in proxy/proxy/provider.py -> _build_exhausted_response() (or wherever the 503 is constructed). Compute the real retry_after as:

  retry_after = max(
      max(unavailable_providers.values()) if unavailable_providers else 0,
      next_available_times_window_edge(),
      next_usage_limit_reset()
  )

### Acceptance Criteria

1. retry_after in the JSON 503 response reflects the **real** next provider availability (not hardcoded 60).
2. A Retry-After HTTP header is set on 503 responses with the same value.
3. The value is the maximum of: cooldown durations, available_times window edges, and usage-limit reset times.
4. If all providers are actually available (edge case), retry_after = 0.
5. Existing tests pass (update any that assert retry_after == 60).
6. Full test suite passes (quiet mode).

### Related work

This is the **proxy-side** half of the fix. The **extension-side** half (Worklog ContextHub) is tracked separately: the Worklog recovery module's classifyError must recognize 'All providers exhausted' and route it to the retry loop with this new Retry-After delay.
data.title: Honest Retry-After: emit real provider availability windows

Follow-up implementation for the KV slot save/restore reuse-gap evaluation (parent LP-0MTAQNB7J0094X71, evaluation-only per AC #5). Created by F5 (LP-0MTCMGJBM007AQ55).

Implements the F4/F5 selected fix set for both modes (fast 3 slots cap 83285 / cheap 2 slots cap 126976):

1. CAP RAISE/RESTORE-PATH FIX (dominant, ~22.8M prefill-tokens/day): ensure persistence applies at the routing clamp for oversized sessions (F2 root cause: 38/48 sessions gated out with 0 saves). Raise session_slot_max_prompt_tokens to per-slot clamp (fast 83285, cheap 126976 — pinned per LP-0MTBTCB8D000OQ0C) AND fix the restore path so accepted sessions actually restore (native checkpoint restores at 4.88%). MUST carry the GPU-wedge plan unchanged (LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO): timeout base 3.0s + 0.0015s/token, max 60s; cooldown 300s after 3 consecutive failures; skip-when-busy stays on.
2. AFFINITY/SLOT-OWNERSHIP FIX (~3.3M): lease churn (166 orphan + 141 evicted releases/day) breaks session-slot continuity (F2); orphan-cleanup continuity + LP-0MSB0RV72001KNRV registry-leak class.
3. RESTORE-BEFORE-SAVE ORDERING (~0.44M): restore before saving for hot same-slot sessions, zero GPU footprint change.
4. /slots 500 + slots_stale fix feeds affinity: router-mode GET /slots 500s (6,865/day, 100% router-proxied per F3) — direct model-instance polling / last-known-state fallback (F3 fix rank 1).

Reference the F1-F5 deliverables: docs/dev/save-restore-reuse-gap-root-cause.md, docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md, docs/dev/restore-rate-metric-fix-ranking.md, docs/dev/mode-specific-recommendation.md; scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py, slot_reuse_gap_analysis.py, slots_500_triage.py, restore_metric_fix_ranking.py, mode_recommendation.py.

## ACs

1. Fast mode serves oversized sessions (up to the 83285 clamp) with persistence: oversized-session save/restore events appear in the corpus for previously-gated sessions.
2. Cheap mode (cap 126976) likewise persists and restores.
3. Native checkpoint restore rate for >50K contexts improves measurably from the 8.6% baseline (F2), within the GPU-wedge plan (no wedges, cooldown fires as configured).
4. GET /slots router 500s reduce (target router:500 == 0 per F3) and slots_stale drops.
5. Full project test suite passes; no regressions; metrics validated by re-running the F1 harness + F4 metric module.

data.description:
Goal: Determine why 76.1% (290/381) of `local_concurrency_limit` fallback events in the 2026-08-28/29 24h window fired while llama-server was generating nothing (0 active local streams), and evaluate concrete ways to reduce local per-request processing time.

Context (from proxy usage analysis, report window 2026-08-28 13:14:52 → 2026-08-29 13:14:52):
- 1293 fallback events; 52.5% (679) fired with 0 active local streams; 99.1% with ≤2 of 3 fast slots.
- `local_concurrency_limit` (381 events, 29.5% of fallbacks) compares the proxy's `local_active_queries` counter (provider.py:_get_local_concurrency_info, line ~1803) against `session_slot_pool_size`. The counter spans the whole request lifecycle at the proxy layer (prompt-eval/prefill, contention-queue waits, lease holds), not just token generation — so it can read "full" while llama-server is idle.
- `Stream started` is logged inside `stream_generator()` (router.py:1092), i.e. at first-byte time, so prompt-eval/prefill time is NOT counted in the report's busy-time metric (27.9% busy). Prefill estimate: median prompt eval ~100 tok/s vs avg-max context ~123389 tokens → potentially ~20 min prefill for the largest prompts.
- Candidate contributors to idle-time counter occupancy: (a) prefill before first token, (b) contention-queue waits (cheap mode queue policy, LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D), (c) no-preemption lease hold/cooldown (router_helpers.py:_try_acquire_local_dispatch, "inactive lease (post-request cooldown) reserves its slot").

Acceptance criteria:
1. Quantified verdict: measure actual prefill time (prompt-eval seconds from llama-server eval-timing lines, total per window) vs decode/busy time, and the distribution of time between `local_active_queries` increment and `Stream started` (first-byte) where derivable; state whether prefill, queue waits, or lease holds dominate the idle-time `local_concurrency_limit` count.
2. Confirm or refute the counter-over-count hypothesis with event-level evidence (e.g. a burst of `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks during a llama-server idle stretch, with no queued work).
3. Evaluate 2-3 concrete levers to improve local processing time (e.g. prefill offloading/batching, adaptive lease timeouts, counting only generating requests toward the pool, prompt-cache positioning to raise warm-cache hit rate) with expected impact quantified from the window data.
4. Recommendation recorded as a comment on this work item with evidence, linked work items (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM etc.), and a proposed follow-up implementation item if warranted.
data.title: Investigate idle-time local_concurrency_limit fallbacks: does local_active_queries over-count busy? Evaluate improving local processing time

Execute the pre-registered design in docs/session-compaction-experiment-design.md (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ): replay tasks drawn from logged sessions through three arms (A uncompacted→remote deepseek-v4-flash baseline, B compacted→local Qwen3, C uncompacted→local ceiling where the clamp allows), score blind on the rubric, and report go/no-go against the pre-registered quality bar (B ≥ 0.95×A rubric, completion B ≥ A−3pp, no failure increase) and efficiency gate (≥25% wasted-prefill reduction; TTFT P95 not >20% worse).

- Task suite: ≥30 tasks/arm/mode trigger–cap band + ≥10 extreme (fast >58.3K / cheap >43K triggers; F3/F4 strategies: fast truncate→≤38K, cheap summarize→≤30K)
- Harness: proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py (eval-only, fixture-tested, reuses analyze_context_distribution/correlate + context_pressure machinery; no speculative infra)
- Arm B via Tier 1 machinery (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD) once implemented, else the harness's manual prompt-assembly pass with before/after logging
- Deliverable: metrics CSV + scored report + go/no-go recommendation; gates Tier 1 enforcement (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD)
## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Task suite extracted from logged sessions meets the pre-registered size bands — ≥30 tasks per arm per mode in the trigger–cap band (fast >58.3K, cheap >43K triggers) and ≥10 extreme tasks per mode (>fast cap / >cheap cap), both modes represented.
- AC2: Harness `proxy/scripts/run_compaction_experiment.py` is eval-only (no behavior change, no dispatch), fixture-tested (pytest), and reuses existing F1/F2 machinery (`analyze_context_distribution.py` / `correlate_oversized_sessions.py` patterns, `context_pressure` estimates) — no speculative infrastructure.
- AC3: Three arms executed against the task suite — A uncompacted→remote deepseek-v4-flash baseline, B compacted→local Qwen3, C uncompacted→local ceiling where the clamp allows; arm B runs through Tier 1 machinery (LP-0MTCWE8NG003P0SD) once implemented, else the harness's manual prompt-assembly pass with before/after compaction logging.
- AC4: Quality bar met — mean rubric score B ≥ 0.95 × A (non-inferiority, α = 0.05), task completion B ≥ A − 3pp (paired lower bound), no failure|gate increase in B vs A (α = 0.05); cap gates in B only for non-compactable extremes.
- AC5: Efficiency gate met or explicitly waived as secondary — wasted-prefill tokens reduced ≥ 25% on the risky population (B vs A) and TTFT P95 in B not > 20% worse than A where the same task is servable locally.
- AC6: Deliverable produced and committed — metrics CSV + scored report + go/no-go recommendation with explicit pre-registered verdict semantics (go: quality bar met + efficiency gate met or waived + compaction event logging present; no-go on any quality bar breach).

data.description:
The muse models on opencode.ai (muse-spark-1.2-contributor, muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free) only work via the OpenAI Responses API (/v1/responses), not /v1/chat/completions. The proxy currently only supports chat/completions.

Goal: Add a configurable api field to remote provider entries that switches the proxy to use the Responses API with automatic request/response translation.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Remote provider config accepts optional api field with values openai-completions (default, current behavior) or openai-responses
2. When api: openai-responses, proxy translates chat/completions request body to responses API format before forwarding (messages → input, max_tokens → max_output_tokens, etc.)
3. Streaming: proxy translates responses API SSE events back to chat/completions SSE format (response.output_text.delta → choices[0].delta.content)
4. Non-streaming: proxy translates responses API JSON response back to chat/completions JSON format
5. All three config files updated: muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free added as first remote fallback after local-qwen3 in the plan chain, using api: openai-responses on endpoint https://opencode.ai/zen/v1
6. Tests cover request translation and response translation
7. Proxy starts successfully with updated configs
data.title: Add OpenAI Responses API support to proxy remote providers
